title: NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own): Waiting Periods and Policy Term Table
content:
## NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own) — Waiting Periods and Policy Term

These are the periods, by tier, that govern when coverage on an NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policy (Write Your Own) attaches and how long one term runs. The standard waiting period runs between the date the application and payment are received and the date coverage attaches, for new business and for coverage increases; the other periods apply under the statutory exceptions named in the table.

| Item | Tenant Contents | Residential Condominium Unit | Manufactured Home | Secondary Single-Family Home | Primary Single-Family Home | Two-to-Four Unit Building |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard waiting period for new business and coverage increases (calendar days) | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 |
| Waiting period when coverage is bought or increased in connection with making, increasing, extending or renewing a loan (calendar days) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Window after a flood map revision that places the building in a Special Flood Hazard Area during which the map-revision exception applies (calendar months) | 13 | 13 | 13 | 13 | 13 | 13 |
| Waiting period under the map-revision exception (calendar days) | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Waiting period when an in-force policy is assigned to the buyer of the building (calendar days) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Length of one policy term (calendar months) | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 |

Every tier carries the same figures: a standard wait of 30 calendar days, no wait (0 days) for a loan transaction, a map-revision window of 13 calendar months with a 1-day wait under that exception, no wait (0 days) on an assignment to the buyer of the building, and a term of 12 calendar months.

### Points of reading

- The waiting periods are counted in calendar days and the map-revision window in calendar months; the term is 12 calendar months long on every tier.
- A figure of 0 days means coverage attaches without any waiting period under that basis; it does not shorten the term.
